title: The Bishop
subtitle: Diagonals only, and always the same color squares.

steps.say: This is the bishop. It moves any number of squares — but only diagonally. Notice something: this bishop starts on a dark square, so it will live on dark squares its whole life.
Watch the bishop glide — corner to corner, always on its own color.

autoMoves.say: ...and all the way into the corner. Fast, elegant — and forever stuck on dark squares. That's why bishops work best in pairs.

steps.prompt: Capture the black pawn with your bishop.
hints: Diagonals only! Which diagonal leads from your bishop to the pawn?

line.say: Perfect — the pawn sat on your bishop's diagonal, three squares away but only one move.

steps.wrongSay: The bishop can't reach that. Trace the diagonal lines leading out of d4.
steps.successSay: Well spotted. Long diagonals are bishop highways.

steps.prompt: Capture all three black pawns — they're all on the bishop's color!
hints: Every pawn here is on a dark square — your bishop can visit them all.
Zigzag: take one pawn, then look for the next one on a new diagonal.

sequenceGoal.say: Got one — now find the diagonal to the next pawn!

steps.wrongSay: No capture there. Each pawn shares a diagonal with your bishop — find it.
steps.successSay: Swept the board! When targets sit on your bishop's color, no distance is safe.

steps.prompt: Two pawns are on your diagonals — one is guarded. Capture the safe one!
hints: Check each target: if you land there, can a black pawn take you back?
The b6 pawn is protected by its neighbor on a7. The e5 pawn is all alone.

line.say: Right — e5 had no defender, so the bishop eats for free.

rejections.say: axb6! The a7 pawn was guarding its neighbor — you just gave away a bishop for a pawn.

steps.wrongSay: There's a free pawn on one of your diagonals. Count defenders before you grab.
steps.successSay: Free pawn, zero regrets. Always count the defenders first.

steps.prompt: Two bishops, one cornered king. Checkmate in one move!
hints: Your king guards a7 and b7, and the dark bishop already watches b8. Only a8 needs an attacker.
Which bishop can hit the long light diagonal ending on a8?

line.say: Checkmate! The light bishop fires down the long diagonal to a8, the dark bishop seals b8, and your king covers the rest.

rejections.say: That eyes a6 — but the king isn't even in check. Aim at the corner square a8 itself.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate — the king still breathes. Find the diagonal that points straight into the a8 corner.
steps.successSay: The two-bishop mate — proof that the pair covers both colors and the whole board.
